didntUnderstand.item: Nudge screen, 'What your description mentions' list: 'Where does the AI come from — mentioned'. I never said where the AI comes from (I only said it calls 'internal systems'), so I don't know what in my sentence counted as a mention. The form also didn't pre-fill that question, which makes the tick look wrong.

Nudge screen: it lists 'What happens with what it produces' under 'Your description doesn't mention' (example 'A person checks each draft before it is used') and shows it as 'not mentioned'. But my sentence says 'without a checkpoint', and the form then pre-fills that exact question quoting 'without a checkpoint'. The two screens contradict each other.

Nudge screen: 'The questions that follow ask about each of these anyway.' It lists 'Whether the people who built it can show why it gave a result' and 'How much weight does what it produces carry' as unmentioned, yet I found no question on either on my form. I didn't understand whether they were skipped on purpose or are missing.

'Places or changes trades': I couldn't tell if 'trades' means financial trades only or any commitment such as a supplier order. I assumed financial and picked 'Something else — sends, books, updates records, deploys changes', but I'm not fully sure.

'Who ends up seeing or receiving what it produces': my orders go to outside suppliers, and no option covers suppliers or other outside businesses ('Clients or customers' and 'The public, the market or regulators' don't fit). I couldn't pick honestly, so I chose Not sure.

'If it gets something wrong, can the mistake be caught and put right...': I don't know the cancellation terms of every supplier, so I couldn't answer confidently. The question assumes I know whether harm is lasting.
'alpha:7b: untested': I don't know what 'untested' means for me, or whether I need to do something about it before relying on the suggestions.
Progress bar step '2 Similar checks' (shown with a back arrow): I didn't see this step or know what it is.

expectNext: I expect Continue to take me to step 4 'Questions', with any follow-up questions the rules need, then step 5 'Confirm' where I can review everything, then step 6 'Result'. The result should say whether I can go ahead with the tool, what is wrong if not, and what needs doing first, with reasons taken from the firm's written rules. I expect it to be fixed rule-matching on my answers, not an AI judgement, so the same answers give the same result. I expect an agent with no human checkpoint to be flagged hard.
ticksMean: 'I've checked this answer' means a person (me) has read what the small local model guessed from my description and agrees it's correct. Until I tick it, or change the answer, the guess doesn't count and I can't continue. So the answer is mine, not the model's, and the model only saves me typing.
comment: The form was mostly easy for a builder like me, but the nudge contradicted itself on two topics and I had no honest answer for who receives supplier orders.
